originality.rationale: The assessed novelty is the position-resolved conditional inversion excess when one specified labeled pair forms a two-cycle. A class-function theorem of Hultman (2013) already contains mean inversions averaged over each conjugacy class and implies the aggregate two-cycle covariance, which is explicitly credited and not claimed original. Neither these class means nor Pinsky’s conditioning on fixed-point count give the specified labeled two-cycle conditional expectation or median-straddling sign diagram. Actual published-finding corpus searches and prior research records claim comparisons did not show this theorem. The result is assessed on best available evidence, not asserted historically unique.

value.rationale: A prescribed two-cycle is the basic local component of the cycle decomposition, while inversion number is a natural global disorder statistic. The exact conditional sign phase diagram identifies which labeled pair placements increase vs decrease global disorder. On a macroscopic half of pair placements the sign differs from the other half; local excesses of order n almost cancel to a prior known aggregate covariance of order one. This resolves a meaningful positional question hidden by conjugacy-averaged descriptions rather than merely recomputing that average.
